objectives: Decode taught short-/e/ CVC words using sound-by-sound blending.
Maintain accurate grapheme-to-phoneme mapping while decoding.
Distinguish short /e/ from previously taught short vowels.
Repair vowel confusions through explicit rereading and blending.
concepts: CVC decoding requires attention to every grapheme.
Short /e/ is represented by e in the taught words.
Blending combines segmented phonemes into a recognizable word.

definitions.definition: Using printed graphemes and their sounds to read a word.
Combining individual phonemes smoothly to produce a word.
A consonant-vowel-consonant word pattern such as bed.

workedExamples: red versus rid → isolate the middle vowel, then blend again.
commonMistakes: Saying isolated sounds without blending them.
revisionPoints: CVC: first sound + vowel sound + final sound.

basic: Blend short-/e/ CVC phonemes into words.
conceptual: Explain why changing the middle vowel changes the word.
application: Decode unfamiliar taught-pattern CVC items without guessing.
higherOrderThinking: Identify and repair a vowel-mapping error during decoding.
mixedReview: Mix short-/e/ words with familiar short-/a/, /i/, and /o/ contrasts.

formulaOrFactBank: CVC decoding = grapheme recognition + phoneme production + blending
mistakeBasedRevision: If e is read as i, isolate the middle sound and remap the printed e before blending.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat short-/e/ sound-by-sound decoding with fresh CVC words.

activities.name: Vowel repair
steps: Present a short-/e/ word and a common misread.

outcomes: Learner accurately decodes taught short-/e/ CVC words.
Learner maintains grapheme-to-phoneme accuracy across all three positions.
Learner distinguishes short /e/ from short /a/, /i/, and /o/ in controlled decoding.
Learner repairs a vowel error by returning to the middle grapheme and blending again.
